summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR2,477 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR180 crore; net debt turned negative at INR11.7 crore.
summary.overview: WeWork India closed its first full year as a listed company with record occupancy (86.9% portfolio, 88.9% mature centres), revenue of INR2,477 crore (+23%), EBITDA of INR499 crore (+23%) and PAT of INR180 crore (+134%). Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR709.9 crore (+29% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 23.2%, a record. Free operating cash flow rose 44% to INR586 crore, FCF after capex was INR129 crore, and the company ended FY26 with net debt negative and a two-notch credit upgrade to A+. Management guided to capacity growth of about 28,000 seats in FY27, with 20,000+ desks of capex-led expansion, and said revenue will grow at over 20% YoY without a formal number.

financial_highlights.change: +42.8% YoY, +22.4% QoQ; margin +231 bps YoY, +218 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore (INR179 crore in another reference)
INR456 crore (INR460 crore cited in Q&A)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR215 crore net debt a year ago

segments.name: Core operations (private and managed offices)
segments.commentary: FY26 core revenue INR2,077 crore (+23%); Q4 core revenue INR584 crore (+29% YoY). Managed office share rose to 21% of revenue in two years.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: FY26 VAS INR295 crore (+36%); Q4 VAS INR95 crore (+35%). Management said VAS typically runs at 12-13% of revenue, and Q4 was lifted by a large customisation deal.

segments.name: Digital products
segments.commentary: FY26 digital revenue INR82 crore (+24%); Q4 INR21 crore (+15%). Includes All Access, Virtual Office, workplace and on-demand.

segments.name: Rivet (design and build)
segments.commentary: New stand-alone design-and-build business for enterprises, landlords and developers, with no WeWork centre commitment and no lease liability. Management said it is not aiming for a large share of revenue; cited a market of USD35-40 billion.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance; management reiterated revenue growth of over 20% YoY, and said earnings growth will be much higher.
Expected FY27 capex of INR500-600 crore for locked-in deals, versus INR456-460 crore in FY26.

Locked-in capacity to about 10.3-10.4 million sq ft (about 155,000 desks) by March 2027, from 8.6 million sq ft today; about 28,000 seats are to be added in FY27, of which 18,000-19,000 are WeWork-branded and about 11,000 are signed managed-office deals.
Management aims to keep portfolio occupancy above 85% through FY27 exit despite capacity additions, and expects a smaller Q1 margin dip than last year.
Management aims to remain net debt negative or close to it at end FY27.
VAS to stay in the 12-13% of revenue range.
FY26 EBITDA margin of 20.2% includes INR9 crore one-time IPO cost; normalised margin 20.5%.
capex_capacity: Operating 8.6 million sq ft across 76 centres; portfolio around 11.6 million sq ft AUM and 110,000 members.
About 36% capacity growth already locked in or signed before FY27 begins.
Q1 FY27 adds about 14,000 desks, of which over 40% is managed office and opens at 100% occupancy; WeWork centres ramp to 85% in about 12 months, with breakeven in 4-6 months.
Capacity grew 16% YoY while members grew 31%. Mature centres are about 87% of capacity at near 90% occupancy; growth centres (under one year) are at 73%.
Q4 FY26 centre-level EBITDA INR212 crore at 31% margin. Portfolio breakeven occupancy 54.8%.
Return on capex about 34% on the recent high-spend deals (JPMorgan and Amazon named as two large deals inflating FY26 capex).
demand_pricing: FY26 desk sales about 48,000 (about 3.3 million sq ft), the highest 12-month velocity, up 20%. More than half of new desks came from existing members expanding.
Revenue-to-rent multiple held at 2.6x (revenue to rent) and 3x (total revenue to rent). Rent per sq ft rose only 0.9% in FY26.
GCCs are about 40% of the existing member base and nearly 50% of new sales in FY26. BFSI and telecom led growth; IT services and pharma declined as a share.
77% of core revenue from enterprises, Fortune 500 at 28%, 65% from global members headquartered outside India, top 10 members about 23% of core revenue.
Average commitment terms rose from 26 to 28 months (from 30 to 33 months for large enterprises). Locked-in core revenue INR2,940 crore (+34%) against locked-in rent INR986 crore.
FY27 opens with INR1,885 crore of core revenue already locked in (36% CAGR over two years).

qa_highlights.question: Is 155,000 seats the operating base by March 2027, and what are the revenue and capex expectations for next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; about 10.3-10.4 million sq ft, roughly 155,000 desks, with potential upside from back-deals. Capex is expected at INR500-600 crore. No revenue guidance; growth over 20% YoY reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: How will Rivet design-and-build differentiate and how large is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a USD35-40 billion market and positioned Rivet as a strategic net to capture overflow and new-city demand for existing clients. It is not aiming for a large share of revenue, and it can reduce external design-build costs in managed office.

qa_highlights.question: What occupancy should the 14,000 Q1 FY27 desks reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Managed-office seats open at 100% occupancy. WeWork seats ramp to about 85% in roughly 12 months, with breakeven in 4-6 months. Growth cohort is already above 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is year-end occupancy on the 27,000-28,000 new seats?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to exit FY27 above 85% occupancy despite dips as capacity comes on. Over 18,000-19,000 of the new seats are WeWork-branded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the portfolio mix change over the next six to eight quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: More premium markets (Bengaluru, Gurgaon, Aerocity) at over INR20,000 per desk, plus growth markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) at INR12,000-18,000 per desk.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the occupancy jump, and how durable is GCC and BFSI demand?
qa_highlights.answer: GCCs are about 40% of members and nearly 50% of FY26 sales. BFSI grew about 200% last year and telecom grew on one large deal. Management said the sector mix will keep shifting.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold in FY27 with capacity coming in?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 will see a smaller dip than last year. Management expects exit margins to expand and FY27 average margins to be similar or slightly higher than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rent escalation exposure on renewals, and how is it passed to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% of assets are expected to renew for another 10 years. Renewal escalations will be higher in some micro-markets, but new deals are repriced to current rents and the revenue-to-rent multiple stays at 2.6-3x.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin dip as 14,000 desks come online; management expects it to be smaller than last year's dip.
Lease renewal escalation: rents are rising in some micro-markets, and rent per sq ft rose only 0.9% in FY26.
FY27 capex of INR500-600 crore against FCF; net debt may move positive during peak capex periods.
Dependence on GCC and BFSI demand; IT services and pharma share declined in FY26.
Q4 VAS was boosted by a one-time customisation deal, so FY27 VAS run-rate may be closer to 12-13% of revenue.
Ramp of 18,000-19,000 new WeWork-branded seats, which carry occupancy risk versus managed offices at 100% occupancy on opening.
Ind-AS versus I-GAAP reconciliation was referenced but not detailed in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed. Management was assertive on demand, margins and cash generation, and deflected on Rivet's scale, services initiatives and detailed revenue guidance, which it declined to give.
key_quotes: FY '26 was our full year as a listed company and we closed it with the strongest set of numbers in our history, record occupancy, revenue, profit and cash.
The business is now self-funding and generating surplus cash of about INR126 crores in FY '26.
Our spaces are filling faster than we're building them.
Rivet is a stand-alone design and build business for enterprises, landlords and developers with no WeWork center commitment required.
